key_insight: An OLS readout on a fixed neural representation can be decomposed exactly into case-level contributions from training examples, linking each action score back to supporting cases and their outcomes.
clinical_relevance: This could make high-stakes AI decisions in medical imaging easier to audit by showing which prior cases influenced a prediction and whether that support is coherent.
method: Fit a linear OLS action probe on top of a frozen neural network representation.
Rewrite each action score as a weighted sum of training-case returns using empirical Gram geometry.
Use the decomposition to trace support, assess action coherence, and flag weak or signed influence.
evidence_signal: Across synthetic CBDT, PJM, Adult Income, and Default Credit tasks, the method achieved the highest mean Top-30 consistency among compared attribution baselines and competitive support reconstruction.
watch_item: Outside the paper’s sufficient CBDT regime, the coefficients are not straightforward similarity-based supports and should be interpreted cautiously as signed Gram-geometric influence.
paper_title: From Neural Network Decisions to Training Cases: An Exact Account via Case-Based Decision Theory
